title: Long DELL — AI Server Earnings Reaction + SNOW Validation
entry: Enter on May 29 open after confirming tonight's Q1 FY2027 earnings. Require: (1) ISG revenue above $19B or AI-optimized server revenue growth ≥80% YoY, (2) FY2027 guide maintained or raised, (3) EPS beat or in-line. Do NOT enter on a miss or a guide cut. If earnings are clean, enter $310–330 at the May 29 open. Scale: 70% at open, 30% add on any intraday pullback to $305–312.
stop_loss: $295 daily close (~7.5% below reference price) — implies AI server demand decelerates or FY2027 guidance is cut
targets: $340 — gap-fill above prior resistance, AI server thesis confirmed by earnings, +6.6%
$370 — SNOW AWS deal read-through fully priced into Dell's AI backlog re-rating, +16.1%
$405 — full ISG AI server supercycle re-rating; analyst target upgrades; $50B AI revenue guide, +27.1%
catalyst: Dell Technologies reports Q1 FY2027 results after the close on May 28, 2026 (conference call 3:30 PM CDT). Consensus: $35.46B revenue (+51.7% YoY), EPS $3.04 (+96% YoY), ISG AI server revenue expected to grow >100% YoY. Dell entered the quarter with a $43B AI backlog (as of Q4 FY2026 exit) and guided FY2027 AI revenue of ~$50B. SNOW's $6B five-year AWS AI expansion deal announced today is the strongest real-time validation of enterprise AI infrastructure spending that directly flows through Dell's ISG order book — AWS is a top-10 Dell AI server customer.
thesis:
Dell is the dominant direct-sale AI server OEM to US enterprise and cloud customers. Its Infrastructure Solutions Group is the single largest beneficiary of the hyperscaler AI capex cycle beyond the chip makers themselves: every NVDA Blackwell GPU cluster that a hyperscaler deploys requires Dell PowerEdge servers, high-speed networking, cooling, and storage — all of which flow through ISG. Dell's Q4 FY2026 AI-optimized server revenue was $9.0B (up 342% YoY), with a $43B backlog and 4,000+ AI customers. The Q1 FY2027 report is the first quarterly confirmation that NVDA's $91B Q2 guide actually materialized as physical server orders flowing through Dell's ISG pipeline.

SNOW's $6B AWS AI deal announced this morning is the most direct corroborating signal available: Snowflake committed $6B to AWS AI infrastructure over five years, and AWS is primarily deploying that on Dell-manufactured clusters in its data centers. Every dollar of hyperscaler AI infrastructure spend ($91B quarterly NVDA + $6B SNOW + an estimated $180B total annual hyperscaler capex) creates downstream demand for Dell's server, networking, and storage products. The ISG segment's backlog of $43B represents approximately 4.8x quarterly revenue at the Q4 FY2026 run rate — the strongest order-book-to-revenue ratio in Dell's history.

The trade setup is post-earnings conditional: enter only after confirming the results meet the stated thresholds. The $295 stop reflects a scenario where Dell misses on AI server growth guidance or provides a below-consensus FY2027 outlook — a genuine negative, not a noise event. The 2-4 week horizon captures the post-earnings positive momentum that typically runs for 10-15 sessions in this type of strong earnings beat cycle. Beyond that window, the June FOMC and SpaceX IPO introduce macro crosscurrents that dilute the single-name earnings thesis.

The key risk is that Dell's AI server margin profile disappoints even if revenue beats: ISG AI margins are thinner than traditional server margins because Dell passes through GPU cost to maintain market share. If Q1 gross margin for AI servers is below 11–12%, the revenue beat may be offset by margin compression, creating a 'revenue beat, stock flat' reaction. Size at 3% (not 4%) to reflect this margin-compression binary.
bull_case: Q1 FY2027 beats on all three dimensions: revenue $36B+, AI server revenue $10B+ (+>100% YoY), EPS $3.20+. FY2027 AI revenue guide raised to $55B+ (vs. $50B prior). SNOW's AWS deal creates a visible demand tail for Dell's compute stack. Stock gaps to $330–340 at the May 29 open and holds. Management calls out HP Enterprise and Cisco losing enterprise AI server share to Dell in the quarter. Target 2 ($370) in reach within 3 weeks on analyst upgrades. Tail: NVDA announces Blackwell Ultra availability pulling forward Dell's rack-level AI cluster orders into Q2.
bear_case: AI server gross margins compress to 10% on competition from HP Enterprise and ODM direct sales; EPS misses despite revenue beat; Dell guides Q2 AI revenue below consensus. Stock falls to $295–310 post-earnings. Stop triggered. Tail: NVDA's $91B Q2 guide raises supply chain fears — if Dell cannot fulfill orders because NVDA allocation is constrained, backlog converts to cancellations rather than revenue, and the entire $43B backlog narrative collapses.
invalidation: $295 daily close, OR ISG AI server revenue growth below 60% YoY in Q1 FY2027 results, OR FY2027 guide cut
